selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the passage say the palace in the comparison stands for?
questions.answer: It stands for this world.

questions.question: What is the first and biggest identification made in that explanation?
questions.answer: The palace is identified as the world.

questions.question: How does the passage connect worship in creation with the identity of the king?
questions.answer: It shows that the One praised by all creatures is the true ruler represented by the king.

questions.question: What does the phrase about many worlds suggest about creation?
questions.answer: It suggests that creation is vast, layered, and richer than what human beings immediately see.

questions.question: What do the foods symbolize, especially those connected with summer and gardens?
questions.answer: They symbolize the visible gifts of mercy provided in creation.

questions.question: What is the role of created beings in relation to those divine names?
questions.answer: Created beings display those names through their order, beauty, and design.

questions.question: Who are his assistants and students in the explanation of the comparison?
questions.answer: His assistants are the prophets, and his students are the saints and purified scholars.

questions.question: Who is that master, according to the passage?
questions.answer: He is Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: Which beings are included among the invited guests?
questions.answer: Jinn, human beings, and animals connected to human life are included.

questions.question: What distinguishes the unbelieving and rebellious group?
questions.answer: They follow Satan and the lower self and reduce life to worldly existence alone.

questions.question: What shift happens at the beginning of the marked passage after the story ends?
questions.answer: The passage moves from the symbolic story to its direct real-world meaning.

questions.question: Who does the king in the comparison represent?
questions.answer: He represents Allah, the eternal sovereign over everything.

questions.question: What does the description of the king teach about Allah’s relation to time?
questions.answer: It teaches that He is not limited by time and is eternal.

questions.question: What are the palace’s many rooms compared to?
questions.answer: They are compared to the many worlds or domains within creation.

questions.question: What deeper lesson is taught by connecting foods with mercy?
questions.answer: The lesson is that provision is not merely material; it is a sign of care from Allah.

questions.question: What do the jewels from unseen treasuries symbolize?
questions.answer: They symbolize manifestations of Allah’s holy names.

questions.question: What role do the prophets, saints, and purified scholars play in this explanation?
questions.answer: They help carry, preserve, and teach the guidance connected to that message.

questions.question: Who are the guests invited to the banquet in the real meaning of the comparison?
questions.answer: They are jinn, human beings, and also animals that serve human beings in this worldly guesthouse.

questions.question: What unseen beings are represented by the servants of the ruler?
questions.answer: They are the angels.

questions.question: What does it mean that they know only the life of this world?
questions.answer: It means they do not recognize the deeper spiritual reality and purpose beyond worldly existence.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the marked passage as a whole?
questions.answer: Its main purpose is to explain what each part of the earlier comparison means in reality.

questions.question: Why does the description of the heavens and the earth support the palace image?
questions.answer: Because both are presented as carefully adorned and arranged, like parts of a royal building.

questions.question: What do the apartments of the palace represent?
questions.answer: They represent the many realms or worlds within creation.

questions.question: What do the many apartments tell us about the structure of creation?
questions.answer: They tell us that creation contains many distinct realms, each arranged appropriately.

title: Transition to Reality Application of the Palace to the World and Statement of the Two Parties
